size.note: Wikipedia gives 15 cm. Newman has no species page.

habitat: Wikipedia says it prefers warm grassland, grassy plain, cornfields and open scrub, and avoids thick forest and hilly country. It runs, flushes with difficulty and flies low before settling again.
summary: Newman has no species page. Wikipedia describes a small running bird, 15 cm, with streaked sandy-brown upperparts, buff underparts, black flank markings and a plain face. In flight a whitish wingbar contrasts with the grey wing. The sexes are similar, and the immature is more spotted below. The female calls hoom-hoom-hoom and the male replies kek-kek-kek. It is a resident. The Kemp name Kurrichane Buttonquail and the code VB were left unchanged.

calls.description: The female calls a deep 'hoom-hoom-hoom' and the male replies 'kek-kek-kek'. No grade A recording was found. The selected file is a grade B call from Bedford in the Eastern Cape. The filename is XC405435-Common Buttonquail.mp3.

research.note: Newman has no species page, so the description and size are from Wikipedia. Avibase lists it as Small Buttonquail and does not mark the Kruger occurrence rare or accidental. Wikipedia calls the species resident, so all twelve months are listed. Sandy-brown is not a vocabulary colour. No grade A recording was found. The grade B call is from the Eastern Cape. The Kemp name Kurrichane Buttonquail and the code VB were left unchanged.
